digest.top_line: AREST: 3yr LRFS 89.2% vs 80.9% (HR 0.52) with adjuvant RT after adequate surgery in pT1-2N0 oral cavity SCC, no OS gain.
digest.tldr: Head/neck carried the day: AREST is the first randomised read on adjuvant RT for margin-negative, node-negative OSCC with intermediate-risk features, and it buys 8.3% absolute LRFS at 3yr with no survival signal and no toxicity reported. Prostate offers the mirror image, a delivery gap: only 67.0% of high-risk pts got guideline-concordant ADT alongside RT.

sites.intro: The adjuvant RT question in pT1-2N0 OSCC finally gets a randomised answer, and the control arm outperformed its own powering assumption.

studies.name: AREST
studies.tldr: 3yr LRFS 89.2% vs 80.9% with adjuvant RT after adequate surgery in pT1-2N0 OSCC, HR 0.52; no OS gain.
details: 🔍 Multicenter open-label phase III RCT from India, N=392 (191 RT vs 201 observation), median f/u 47.2mo
🔍 Eligibility: pT1-2 pN0 OSCC after adequate surgery (margins ≥5mm, ipsilateral level I-III neck dissection with ≥16 nodes)
🔍 Intermediate-risk features required: DOI ≥5 to ≤10mm, PNI, LVE, or poor differentiation
📐 RT arm: 60Gy/30fx over 6 weeks to tumor bed and at-risk neck nodal region

details.text: 📊 LRFS and loco-regional failure, ITT vs per-protocol

details: 📊 DFS and OS not significantly different between arms; no effect sizes reported in source
⚠️ 8.3% absolute LRFS gain, NNT ~12 to prevent one loco-regional event at 3yr, against 6 weeks of RT
⚠️ Oral tongue benefit over buccal mucosa is labeled exploratory in source; subgroup HR not reported in source text
⚠️ No toxicity data in source abstract or slide, so the xerostomia/trismus cost of 60Gy is unquantified here
🔗 Powered on an assumed 3yr LRFS of 70% in the observation arm; observed control arm did far better at 80.9%, shrinking the absolute room the trial had to move

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase III, prespecified LRFS primary hit, adequate f/u, replaces retrospective-only evidence for this exact decision. OS-neutral, so magnitude gates adoption, not validity.
verdict.audience: pT1-2 pN0 OSCC, adequately resected, ≥1 intermediate risk factor (DOI 5-10mm,…

studies.significance: The RT question here is finally randomised: 60Gy/30fx to tumor bed plus at-risk neck cuts 3yr loco-regional failure from 18.9% to 10.6%, an 8.3-point LRFS gain with no DFS or OS movement at 47.2mo. Surgical adequacy was strictly defined (≥5mm margins, ≥16 nodes), so the result only transfers where the neck was properly dissected.
studies.monday_clinic: In an adequately resected pT1-2N0 oral cavity SCC with PNI, LVE, DOI 5-10mm or poor differentiation, this supports offering adjuvant RT for loco-regional control while being explicit that survival did not move; it does not apply to node-positive disease, close or positive margins, or an inadequate neck dissection.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Multicenter, open-label, phase III RCT** from India, 1:1 randomization stratified by oral cavity subsite, PNI/LVE and differentiation. **N=392** (191 RT, 201 observation), median follow-up **47.2 months** (IQR 30-59.4). Powered at 80% (α 0.05) to detect **HR 0.6256**, assuming 3yr LRFS of 70% in the observation arm.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Early-stage pT1-T2, pN0 OSCC** after adequate surgery, defined as **clear margins ≥5mm** plus at least ipsilateral level I-III neck dissection yielding **≥16 nodes**. Required **≥1 intermediate risk factor**: DOI ≥5 to ≤10mm, perineural invasion, lymphovascular emboli, or poor differentiation. Baseline characteristics balanced.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **60Gy in 30 fractions over 6 weeks** to the **resected tumor bed and at-risk neck nodal region**. Conventional fractionation, standard postoperative dose; no dose-escalated or hypofractionated arm.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: LRFS**, from randomization to first documented local and/or regional recurrence of the index cancer. Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, reported as 3-year point estimates with 95% CI. Secondary reporting covered cumulative incidence of loco-regional failure with death as competing event, DFS and OS.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Primary endpoint met in both ITT and per-protocol analyses; **DFS and OS were not significantly different** between arms. The trial's own subgroup read placed **oral tongue** above buccal mucosa for RT benefit, and the slide labels that finding **exploratory**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: This is the first randomised answer to a question previously carried by retrospective series, and it lands in the same place they did on direction: RT buys loco-regional control in intermediate-risk pN0 disease. The observation arm outperformed the 70% design assumption at **80.9%**, so the modern well-staged neck fails less than the historical literature predicted.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents adequately resected pT1-2 pN0 oral cavity SCC carrying at least one intermediate risk factor. Does not represent node-positive disease, close or positive margins, DOI >10mm, or a neck that was not dissected to level I-III with ≥16 nodes.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Open-label with no reported toxicity or QoL data in the source, so the late RT cost (xerostomia, trismus, fibrosis) that a patient weighs against an 8.3-point control gain is not quantified. The oral-tongue advantage is exploratory and the subgroup HR is not reported in source text, so it cannot yet select who to treat. Follow-up at 47.2mo is short for a survival endpoint in early oral cavity disease.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The trial converts a retrospective-evidence decision into a randomised one, but the currency is loco-regional control rather than survival, so the conversation with the patient is about avoiding salvage surgery and its morbidity, not living longer. With 18.9% failure under observation, most patients treated do not need the RT, and salvage remains possible for some who recur.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 60Gy/30fx to tumor bed plus at-risk neck lowers 3yr loco-regional failure from 18.9% to 10.6% in adequately resected pT1-2N0 OSCC with an intermediate risk factor. Conventional dose and target, so it transfers directly. The decision is offering PORT to a node-negative neck, previously retrospective-only.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: The eligibility gate is surgical: margins ≥5mm and level I-III dissection with ≥16 nodes. A neck resected to that standard still failed 18.9% at 3yr with intermediate-risk pathology, so operative adequacy alone does not close the risk, and the pathology report (DOI 5-10mm, PNI, LVE, differentiation) becomes the referral trigger.

open_questions: Which intermediate risk factor alone justifies RT
Whether oral tongue benefit holds prospectively
Late toxicity cost of 60Gy against 8.3% control gain

sites.intro: Not a trial result but a practice audit: what RT patients actually get prescribed alongside definitive treatment, and how much of it varies by center rather than by risk.

studies.name: MROQC ADT Practice Patterns
studies.tldr: 67.0% of 553 high-risk pts got guideline-concordant ADT (≥18mo); ARPI use 23.2% among STAMPEDE-eligible post-publication.
details: 📊 553 pts, 26 Michigan centers, June 2020 to Nov 2024; 91.3% recommended any ADT, 67.0% guideline-concordant (≥18mo)
🔍 Prospective statewide consortium (MROQC) capture of INTENDED ADT duration + ARPI use, not delivered duration

details.text: 📊 Predictors of guideline-concordant ADT on MVA

details: 📐 Facility-level variability persisted after adjustment for clinical factors, P<.0001
📊 Cohort composition: GG 4-5 75.0%, PSA ≥20 40.0%, cN1 19.9%, cT3/4 13.3%
📊 27.9% met STAMPEDE M0 criteria; ARPI recommendation went 0% pre-publication to 23.2% after
⚠️ Intended duration is the outcome, so real-world early discontinuation would push true concordance below 67.0%
⚠️ Michigan-only consortium of self-selected quality-reporting centers; national concordance plausibly lower
⚠️ Guideline non-concordance is not automatically undertreatment: comorbidity and pt preference are not reported as adjudicated reasons in the abstract

verdict.rationale: Prospective practice-pattern survey, no efficacy endpoint. Describes what radiation oncologists recommend, not whether any duration or intensification strategy performs better.
verdict.audience: Intact high-risk M0/N0-1 prostate ca planned for definitive RT

studies.significance: Facility remained an independent driver of ADT duration after adjusting for cN1, grade group and PSA (P<.0001), so where a man is treated shifts his hormone exposure more than the guideline does. The ARPI gap is starker: 0% to 23.2% uptake among the 27.9% who were STAMPEDE M0-eligible, meaning three quarters of eligible high-risk pts on definitive RT are not offered intensification.
studies.monday_clinic: In intact high-risk M0 disease meeting STAMPEDE M0 criteria (≥2 of cT3/T4, GG 4-5, PSA ≥40, or cN1), this documents that ARPI intensification is being recommended in under a quarter of eligible pts; it says nothing about outcomes for pts outside those criteria.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective observational cohort drawn from the **Michigan Radiation Oncology Quality Consortium (MROQC)**, a statewide quality collaborative. Clinical data and **intended** ADT duration and ARPI use were collected prospectively at the point of care rather than abstracted retrospectively.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **553 pts** across **26 centers**, enrolled June 2020 to November 2024, with intact high-risk **M0/N0-1** prostate cancer planned for definitive radiotherapy. Risk composition: GG 4-5 in **75.0%**, PSA ≥20 ng/mL in **40.0%**, cN1 in **19.9%**, cT3/4 in **13.3%**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** intended guideline-concordant ADT, defined as **≥18 months**, per the 2022 AUA/ASTRO recommendation of 18-36 months. Secondary analyses covered multivariable predictors of concordance, facility-level variability via a mixed-effects model with treatment site as random intercept, and ARPI adoption before versus after STAMPEDE M0 publication.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **91.3%** were recommended ADT but only **67.0%** at a guideline-concordant duration. Concordance tracked disease burden (cN1, GG 4-5, PSA ≥40), yet **facility-level variability persisted in the MVA (P<.0001)**. Among the **27.9%** meeting STAMPEDE criteria, ARPI recommendation rose from **0%** to **23.2%** after publication.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents intact high-risk M0/N0-1 prostate cancer treated with definitive radiotherapy at Michigan consortium centers. Does not represent post-prostatectomy salvage, node-positive M1 disease, or practice outside a participating quality collaborative.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The outcome is the **intended** recommendation captured at planning, so attrition, toxicity-driven early cessation and pt refusal are invisible; delivered concordance is likely lower than 67.0%. Membership in a quality consortium is itself a selection effect toward guideline adherence, and no adjudicated reason for shorter duration (comorbidity, competing risk, pt preference) is reported, so the 33% non-concordant fraction cannot be split into justified de-escalation versus undertreatment.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The MVA reads as clinicians titrating ADT to perceived risk rather than applying a flat guideline threshold, which is defensible individually but leaves site of care as an unexplained variance source. The ARPI signal is the more actionable finding: STAMPEDE M0 moved recommendations off zero within the study window, but the ceiling at 23.2% suggests diffusion into the definitive-RT setting is early rather than complete.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This is a radiation oncology practice audit: ADT duration alongside definitive RT is the rad onc's own prescription, and facility remained significant after adjustment (P<.0001), so the driver is departmental habit rather than case mix. With 67.0% concordance and ARPI at 23.2% among STAMPEDE-eligible pts, the actionable step is auditing your own intended durations against the 18-36 month guideline.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: ARPI intensification for high-risk M0 disease is being recommended in only 23.2% of the 27.9% who meet STAMPEDE M0 criteria, up from 0% pre-publication. That gap sits at the RT/systemic interface, so med onc co-management at the point of RT planning, not at recurrence, is where eligible pts are currently being missed.

open_questions: Does intended ADT duration match delivered duration in this cohort?
What drives facility-level variability after clinical adjustment?
Has ARPI uptake risen beyond 23.2% since November 2024?

papers.title: Androgen Deprivation Therapy Practice Patterns in High-Risk Prostate Cancer Treated With Definitive Radiotherapy: Prospective Results From a Statewide Quality Consortium
papers.abstract: PURPOSE The 2022 AUA/ASTRO guidelines recommend 18-36 months of androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) with definitive radiotherapy for localized, high-risk prostate cancer. The STAMPEDE M0 trial supports intensification with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) for patients with ≥2 cT3/T4, Grade Group [GG] 4-5, prostate-specific antigen (PSA) ≥40 ng/mL, or cN1. Given advances in imaging, risk stratification, and treatment delivery, we characterized contemporary practice patterns using prospective data from the Michigan Radiation Oncology Quality Consortium (MROQC). METHODS Patients enrolled in MROQC with intact, high-risk M0/N0-1 prostate cancer were included. Clinical information, including intended ADT duration and ARPI use, was prospectively collected. The primary outcome was intended guideline-concordant ADT (GC-ADT, ≥18 months). Multivariable analyses (MVA) assessed associations between clinical factors and GC-ADT recommendations. We compared the adoption of ARPI with standard therapies before and after the publication of STAMPEDE M0. Facility-level variability was evaluated using a mixed-effects model, with the treatment site as a random intercept. RESULTS Between June 2020 and November 2024, 553 patients across 26 centers were included: cT3/4 (13.3%), cN1 (19.9%), GG 4-5 (75.0%), and PSA ≥20 ng/mL (40.0%). Overall, 91.3% were recommended ADT, with 67.0% being guideline-concordant. On MVA, GC-ADT was significantly associated with cN1 (odds ratio [OR], 2.94 [95% CI, 1.44 to 5.99]), GG (GG4 OR, 6.23 [95% CI, 2.85 to 13.62]; GG5 OR, 9.45 [95% CI, 4.46 to 20.06]), and PSA ≥40 (OR, 3.64 [95% CI, 1.22–10.87]). Facility-level variability persisted in the MVA ( P < .0001). Among the 27.9% who met meeting STAMPEDE criteria, ARPI recommendations increased from 0% prepublication to 23.2% afterward. CONCLUSION Within a statewide quality consortium, guideline-concordant ADT recommendations occurred in two thirds of patients, with ARPI intensification in under 25% among STAMPEDE-eligible patients. These findings highlight the need for individualized ADT strategies and collaborative efforts to standardize high-quality care.

papers.title: Adjuvant radiotherapy versus observation following curative surgery for early-stage oral squamous cell carcinoma (AREST; CTRI/2017/07/009114).
authors: AREST Study - Head and Neck Cooperative Oncology Group
papers.abstract: 6000 Background: The role of adjuvant radiotherapy (RT) in early-stage, node-negative oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) with one or more intermediate risk factors - such as depth of invasion (DOI) ≥5 to ≤10mm, perineural invasion (PNI), lymphovascular emboli (LVE), or poor differentiation - remains debatable and is largely based on retrospective data. This multicenter, open-label, phase III randomized controlled trial was designed to assess the impact of post-operative adjuvant RT in this setting. Methods: Patients with early-stage (pT1-T2), node-negative (pN0) OSCC undergoing adequate surgery (defined as clear margins ≥5mm and at least ipsilateral level I-III neck dissection with ≥16 nodes) with presence of one or more intermediate risk factors were screened. Eligible patients underwent stratified randomization (oral cavity subsite, PNI/LVE, and differentiation) in 1:1 ratio to either observation or adjuvant RT (60Gy in 30 fractions over 6-weeks) to the resected tumor-bed and at-risk neck nodal region after written informed consent. Primary endpoint was loco-regional recurrence-free survival (LRFS) measured from randomization to first documented event of local and/or regional recurrence from index cancer. All time-to-event outcomes were computed using Kaplan-Meier (KM) method with log-rank test for comparison and expressed as 3-year point estimates with 95% confidence intervals (CI). The planned sample size (N=392) provided 80% power at an α of 0.05 to detect a Hazard Ratio (HR) of 0.6256, assuming 3-year LRFS of 70% in the observation arm. Results: Following curative surgery, a total of 392 patients were randomized (191 to adjuvant RT; 201 to observation). Baseline characteristics were balanced between the two arms. At a median follow-up of 47.2 months (inter-quartile range=30-59.4 months), 3-year KM estimate of LRFS was 89.2% in adjuvant RT arm vs 80.9% in observation arm (HR=0.52, 95%CI=0.30-0.91; p=0.02) in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population and 91.1% vs 80.9% (HR=0.43, 95%CI=0.23-0.80; p=0.01) on per-protocol (PP) analyses. Cumulative incidence of loco-regional failure with death as competing event was 10.6% (95%CI=6.1%-15.1%) with adjuvant RT and 18.9% (95%CI=13.3%-24.6%) with observation (HR=0.52, 95%CI=0.30-0.91; p=0.021) in the ITT population and 8.7% (95%CI=4.3%-13.1%) vs 18.9% (95%CI=13.3%-24.6%) (HR=0.43, 95%CI=0.23-0.79; p=0.007) on PP analyses. Disease-free and overall survival were not significantly different between the two arms. Subgroup analysis identified oral tongue deriving higher benefit of adjuvant RT compared to buccal mucosa. Conclusions: Adjuvant RT significantly reduces risk of loco-regional recurrence for early-stage, node-negative adequately resected OSCC, particularly oral tongue. However, such reduction in loco-regional failure does not translate into significant survival benefit. Clinical trial information: CTRI/2017/07/009114.
